Consider the ellipse centered at the origin with horizontal radius $10$ and vertical radius $4,$ as shown above. Construct a set of parametric equations, defined for $\theta \in [0,2\pi ),$ that traverse the ellipse once in the counterclockwise direction starting at the point $I(10,0).$

$x=$ 
{{field-1}}$,\,y=$ 
{{field-2}}$,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).$
question.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of an ellipse centered at the origin with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ are

$$
x=a\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=b\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

Under this parametrization, the ellipse is traversed once in the counterclockwise direction, starting from $(a,0).$

In our case, $a=10$ and $b=4.$ Therefore, the parametric equations of the ellipse are

$$
x=10\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$
